name: Glacian
body:
Glacians are hardy, tribal people adapted to life in frigid and challenging polar environments where they traverse the icy surfaces of enormous icebergs with ease and swim adeptly through the frozen sea hunting seals with the grace and prowess of mighty polar bears.

Physical Description

Glacians are easily recognized by their purple-hued skin tones and unique eyes.

The eyes of a glacian have no whites—they are entirely blue, looking like pools of rippling water with slim black pupil slits floating in the center. It’s nearly impossible not to be mesmerized by a glacian’s vibrant blue gaze. A tiny portion of the glacian population is born with albinism, having snow-white skin and purple eyes.

Glacians run the gamut from four and a half to six and a half feet tall, with the majority falling between five to six feet. They weigh anywhere from 95 to 300 pounds.

Regardless of whether glacians are short or tall or thick or thin, they are physically and mentally equipped to meet the rigors of living in an inhospitable environment.

Glacians stubbornly refuse to give up, even under the most challenging and seemingly hopeless situations.

Society

Glacians live in tight knit tribal groups amid extended families with multiple generations sharing shelter, provisions, and responsibilities. Exposure to cultures outside of their own is minimal, limited primarily by two major factors of their glacial existence. First, vegetation and game animals are sparse, providing little excess bounty to attract prolific trade. Second, the poles are difficult to reach being situated in remote regions of the globe and accessed by long voyages over open seas or across inhospitable, treacherous, snow-covered wilderness.

Because glacians encounter so few individuals outside of their immediate clans, they are cautious of strangers. Once a newcomer establishes trust and is accepted into a tribal unit, however, they can expect nothing but fierce loyalty from their glacian friends. Glacians will risk everything to secure the safety of one of their tribe.

Relations

Few creatures populate the frozen wilderness (besides the glacians, the penguins, and the polar bears!) resulting in minimal exposure to other races for the glacians. On the rare occasions when a seafaring vessel arrives at their shores, glacians are happy to exchange furs and whalebone for other useful trade goods.

Glacians treat honest traders with respect and an appreciation for their ability to brave the challenges of piloting a vessel amid the hazardous ice flows in the region.

Glacians hate frost giants. As soon as they can wield a weapon, they are taught how best to defend themselves against the ruthless raiders. Frost giants frequently steal stores of whale blubber and seal meat, leaving glacian settlements short on food.

Worst of all, frost giants often abduct glacians for slaves. A glacian would rather die fighting a frost giant than risk being taken captive by one to live a life of captivity and abuse.

Alignment And Religion

Glacians live day to day, surviving on their wits and grit in an environment devoid of over abundance. As a self-sufficient society, most glacians put their faith in their own physical prowess and that of their kin to successfully provide for their needs and keep themselves safe. Glacians that turn to deities to influence their fate favor gods of the sea, with a secondary preference for gods of strength, hunting, winter, or bears.

Most glacians are considerate, cooperative, and family oriented which definitely works in their favor considering they live in tight quarters amongst several generations of their kin. They also favor order over disorder. Without proper preparations and careful attention to detail, it’s too easy to perish in the unforgiving habitat that is their home. Glacians that break the law or endanger the welfare of the tribe are swiftly punished. Murderers are promptly banished to the wilderness to meet their death, naked and unarmed. Threats from harsh living conditions are numerous and lethal enough to glacian survival that violence from community members is not tolerated at all.

Adventurers

The majority of Glacians know nothing other than their way of life and are content to be a contributing member of their tribe.

Occasionally, a glacian is born with an insatiable curiosity that drives them to travel beyond the horizon to distant lands. These glacians are rare. Indeed, most people will never see a glacian in their entire lives.

A glacian enslaved by frost giants might be relocated far from home. If able to escape, the newly freed glacian may end up lost or enticed to explore the unfamiliar surroundings they find themselves in.

Finally, during the years of the foulpox plague when the glacian tribes were decimated by the mysterious disease, many of the strongest and healthiest glacians were dispatched to foreign communities seeking information about the plague’s cause and possible treatments. Some of these emissaries became enamored with the new lands they visited and chose to return to them after the emergency passed.

Luckily for the viability of the glacian race, the foulpox outbreak ended as mysteriously as it began. It never resurfaced, and to this day, no one knows what caused the exploding, foul-smelling red blisters that covered a victim’s body in the hours before they bled to death from liver hemorrhaging.

Naming Conventions: Male names always end in a consonant and female names always end in a vowel.

Male Names: Anook, Beartik, Beartrom, Krom, Orik, Orsten, Svedick, Urick, Vitner, Volfer.

Female Names: Aanu, Anika, Anyanka, Asla, Eisla, Gilda, Katya, Kia, Livia, Luma, Nya, Reenia, Revna.

Glacian Racial Traits
Type: Glacians are humanoids with the glacian subtype.
Ability Score Modifiers: Glacians have an uncanny understanding of nature’s workings and a body fortified against the rigors of wilderness living. This combination makes them well-equipped to live in the harsh glacial regions of the world. However, life in these remote, sparsely populated areas doesn’t provide many opportunities to hone interpersonal skills. They gain +2 Constitution and Wisdom, but suffer -2 to Charisma
Size: Medium. Glacians are Medium creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.
Speed: Normal. Glacians have a base speed of 30 feet.
Senses: Darkvision 60 ft. Glacians are adapted to the long stretches of darkness during the polar winters; they can see in the dark up to 60 feet.
Languages: Glacians begin play speaking Common and glacian. Glacians with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Aquan, Giant, Orc, and Sylvan.
Survival Training: Glacians have a +1 dodge bonus to Armor Class and Reflex saving throws.
Frontier Survivor: Glacians have a +1 racial bonus on Fortitude and Will saving throws.
Glacier Born: Glacians are naturally tolerant of frigid temperatures but susceptible to blistering heat; they automatically succeed on saving throw rolls to avoid the effects of extreme cold (as though protected by endure elements) and have cold resistance 1, but they suffer a -1 penalty on saving throw rolls made to avoid the effects of extreme heat. Additionally, glacians can move across icy and snowy surfaces without penalty, though they still need to make Acrobatics checks to run or charge across these surfaces.
Oceanic Hunter: Glacians have a swim speed of 30 feet (with a +8 racial bonus on Swim checks) and they can hold their breath for 1 hour + a number of rounds equal to four times their Constitution score before risking drowning or suffocating.
Alternate Racial Traits

The following racial traits may be selected instead of the standard racial traits for glacian characters.

Ancestral Lorekeeper: Some glacians are called upon to be their tribe’s historian, focusing less on martial pursuits and more on teaching the new generation their cultural stories, dances, and music. These glacians receive 1 extra skill point per level which must be spent on Performance (any). (The Performance skill selected doesn’t need to be the same at each new level.)

This replaces survival training.

Furred Warrior: Some glacians are born without the natural ability to withstand frigid temperatures. They become accustomed to the bulk and weight of furs and multiple layers of clothing. These Galatians reduce the armor check penalty of any light, non-metal armor they wear by 1.

This replaces glacial born.

Sworn Enemy: As soon as they can wield a weapon, glacians are taught how best to survive a battle against their two most destructive enemies—white dragons and frost giants. They gain a +1 racial bonus on attack rolls against creatures with the dragon and giant subtypes. This replaces frontier survivor.

Wild Soul: Glacians are vigilant and resourceful. They are quick to notice threats to their survival and can stretch limited resources further than most. They have a +1 racial bonus on Knowledge (Nature), Perception, and Survival checks. This replaces survival training.

Whale Hunter: Some glacians are slower swimmers than their brethren and don’t have an enhanced lung capacity so they do more of their nautical hunting via boats rather than underwater. These glacians have a 15 foot swim speed and have proficiency with the harpooneu. They are particularly adept at fighting big prey, gaining a +1 racial bonus on attack rolls made against creatures that are Gargantuan or larger. This replaces oceanic hunter.

Lost Atlanteans, Copyright 2024, Bloodstone Press; author Beth Jones
